summary:
Welcome to Mission Beninging, where tomorrow's astronauts discover that surviving on the Moon involves more than planting flags and eating freeze-dried snacks!

Our concept is a humorous, browser-based educational game that puts young astronauts in charge of a lunar outpost. Players must balance limited electricity, oxygen, water, food production, and radiation protection while dealing with unexpected emergencies.

Every decision matters. Should you use your last units of energy to produce oxygen, grow potatoes, or protect your crew from a solar storm?

Inspired by NASA educational resources on lunar conditions and life-support systems, the game aims to introduce systems thinking, engineering trade-offs, and space exploration through playful decision-making.

Our motto: "One small step for mankind, one giant mistake for our potatoes."

This submission describes an initial concept created to test the NASA Space Apps submission process.
details:
The Challenge

Living on the Moon or Mars requires careful management of essential resources. Astronauts must maintain life support, generate energy, produce food, and protect themselves from environmental hazards.

We want to introduce these challenges to young learners in an accessible and entertaining way.

Our Proposed Solution

Mission Beninging is a concept for an interactive mission simulator in which players become commanders of a small lunar base.

Players would manage five interconnected systems:

  • Oxygen: Keep the crew breathing.
  • Power: Allocate electricity among essential systems.
  • Water: Manage consumption and recycling.
  • Food: Maintain a tiny greenhouse growing the galaxy's most important potatoes.
  • Radiation Protection: Keep astronauts safe during hazardous space-weather events.

Gameplay

Each round represents one day on the Moon.

Players make decisions about resource allocation, encounter random mission events, and see how their choices affect survival.

Possible events include:

  • A solar storm threatens the habitat.
  • An oxygen generator malfunctions.
  • The greenhouse loses power.
  • A mysterious potato disappears.
  • Mission Control sends an extremely unhelpful message.

Players earn points for maintaining crew health, conserving resources, and successfully completing their mission.

Proposed Technical Approach

The application could be developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript as a browser-based educational game.

Its simulation would rely on simplified resource balances and decision-making rules, with educational explanations inspired by NASA's published information about lunar environments and spacecraft life-support systems.

The simplified game parameters would be clearly distinguished from real engineering measurements.

Educational Impact

The concept targets students approximately 10–16 years old, encouraging them to explore aerospace engineering, systems thinking, resource constraints, and teamwork.

The objective is to make difficult engineering concepts engaging and memorable.

Current Status

This is an initial concept and submission-workflow test. A functional simulation, validated numerical model, and playable demonstration have not yet been developed.
